Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
lowering this into a usable request because the access list at North Loop Shared Studio has gotten hard to follow, and i want a practical proposal for reviewing and maintaining it, not a decision about anyone's access. the studio is on one floor and has 28 members and six staff. there are three work rooms, one front entrance and a rear loading door. members use badges; there isn't a keypad code to include. the rear door matters for equipment deliveries, so don't treat the two doors as interchangeable in the proposal.

Nia Patel, the studio coordinator, maintains a Google sheet. it has tabs named Current, Paused, and Contractors, and it was last reconciled on October 3, 2025. The rows include a person's name, email, phone number, badge ID, door scope, sponsor, and review date. Some sponsor cells are blank. There are four shared loan badges; two are labeled "Guest". Badge activity records are available for 90 days. I don't have a count of how many rows are incomplete, and i don't want you to assume one or fill anything in. A visiting photographer who used the studio last season is still listed, but we have not confirmed whether that person has used a badge since then. Don't infer from the list alone that the person should be removed or still needs access.

We have been hearing a mix of practical comments and worries, and these should stay in the request as quoted remarks, not be converted into policy: "The rear door is for carts, not a shortcut after midnight." "I can cover the Tuesday close, but I can't own every badge question." "Please don't delete a name just because the log is quiet." The comments came up while people were discussing deliveries, end-of-day coverage, and the access list, not as a formal vote. Please include them exactly if the proposal refers to the discussion. Also there is a note from a coordinator's handoff, copied here exactly: "Nia: compare the Current and Paused tabs before sending review reminders; a leave date may be in the notes column." Keep that note whole; it points to a useful cross-check, but it doesn't mean every paused person should be contacted.

What i need is a clear proposal the studio can use to make the list easier to review without changing anyone's access as part of the proposal. It should say who does what in a normal review, what information someone checks, and how missing details or conflicting entries are raised for follow-up. Nia is currently the maintainer, but the six staff share closing coverage and there isn't a named backup for the sheet. Don't make up a new job title or say a staff member has agreed to take over. It would help if the proposal made it possible to see the distinction between a routine check and an actual request to add, change, or end someone's badge access.

Please organize the request into a practical set of steps. Cover checking the names and badge IDs across all three tabs, comparing door scope with the person's current studio role or arrangement when that information is available, and recording a review date. Include a way to flag blank sponsor fields and apparent duplicates rather than silently guessing what belongs there. The sheet may contain personal contact details, so the proposal should not suggest copying the whole sheet into an open channel or circulating it to people who don't need it. Don't add technical tools, a retention schedule, or a new access rule that i haven't specified.

The activity records go back 90 days, but quiet activity alone isn't a reason to remove somebody. If a member has no badge activity in 60 days, flag the entry for a manager check; do not remove access automatically. That's an important condition, and please carry it through wherever you describe review or escalation. If a scheduled residency or an approved leave runs past the 60-day point, note the relevant end date and hold the entry for review until then rather than treating inactivity as a conclusion. The handoff note about a possible leave date should be used as a reason to check the notes column, not as confirmation that leave applies to a particular person.

There are four loan badges and two currently have the label "Guest". I need the proposal to explain how those shared badges can be checked and documented, including how someone could report that a badge label or assignment seems unclear. It should not assume that the two Guest labels identify particular people, that loan badges belong to a permanent member, or that all four are presently in use. The proposal can identify questions for the studio to resolve, but it shouldn't answer those questions by inventing assignments. Include the rear loading door in the review because it has a specific delivery purpose, and retain the quoted remark about it without turning that remark into a new restriction.

Please give the finished prompt a useful title and ask for a concise but usable proposal, with a short opening summary, a numbered review workflow, and a final section of unresolved questions or information to confirm. In that numbered section, cover: 1) preparing and checking the sheet, 2) handling missing or conflicting details and the 60-day condition, and 3) documenting follow-up without making access changes. Then include a small sample review record using clearly fictional placeholder values, not any real person's email, phone, name, or badge ID. It needs fields corresponding to the sheet's name, email, phone number, badge ID, door scope, sponsor, and review date, and it should show how an unknown value is marked as needing follow-up rather than guessed. Don't create actual entries for the photographer or any other person.

The result should be easy for Nia and the closing staff to understand and use, but don't present the remarks as unanimous agreement, claim a process has been approved, or decide who gets access. End with a substantive section listing what the studio still needs to confirm, including who can make an access change, who can serve as backup maintainer, how blank sponsors should be resolved, and what to do when a badge record conflicts with the tabs. Keep that as open questions rather than supplying answers. The point is to organize a careful review request from the facts above, not to write to members, edit the sheet, or conduct the review.", "output": "# Prompt: Proposal for Reviewing the North Loop Shared Studio Access List

Prepare a concise, practical proposal for reviewing and maintaining the North Loop Shared Studio access list. The proposal should make the list easier to review without changing anyone’s access or deciding whether any individual should retain access. Do not conduct the review, edit the sheet, contact members, or invent missing information, assignments, roles, or decisions.

## Studio and list context

North Loop Shared Studio is on one floor and has 28 members, six staff, three work rooms, a front entrance, and a rear loading door. Members use badges; there is no keypad code to include. The rear door is used for equipment deliveries, so distinguish it from the front entrance in the proposal.

Studio coordinator Nia Patel maintains a Google sheet with tabs named Current, Paused, and Contractors. It was last reconciled on October 3, 2025. Its rows include a person’s name, email, phone number, badge ID, door scope, sponsor, and review date. Some sponsor fields are blank. Four shared loan badges exist, and two are labeled “Guest.” Badge activity records are available for 90 days. The number of incomplete rows is unknown; do not estimate it or fill in missing values. A visiting photographer who used the studio last season remains listed, but it has not been confirmed whether that person has used a badge since then. Do not infer from the list alone whether that person should retain or lose access.

The six staff share closing coverage, but no backup maintainer for the sheet has been named. Nia is the current maintainer. Do not invent a new job title or state that anyone has agreed to take over. The proposal should distinguish routine list review from an actual request to add, change, or end badge access.

## Required review workflow

Provide a numbered workflow that covers:

1. Preparing and checking the sheet, including comparing names and badge IDs across Current, Paused, and Contractors; checking door scope against a person’s current studio role or arrangement when that information is available; and recording a review date.
2. Handling missing or conflicting details. Flag blank sponsor fields and apparent duplicates for follow-up rather than guessing or silently changing them. Explain how unclear loan-badge labels or assignments can be reported and documented without assuming that either “Guest” label identifies a particular person, that a loan badge belongs to a permanent member, or that all four loan badges are in use.
3. Documenting follow-up without making access changes. Explain how the process distinguishes a routine check from a request for an access change. Do not recommend copying the full sheet into an open channel or circulating it to people who do not need it, since the sheet may contain personal contact details. Do not add technical tools, a retention schedule, or a new access rule.

Badge activity records cover 90 days. If a member has no badge activity in 60 days, flag the entry for a manager check; do not remove access automatically. Carry this condition through the review and escalation steps. If a scheduled residency or approved leave runs past the 60-day point, note the relevant end date and hold the entry for review until then rather than treating inactivity as a conclusion. Use the handoff note about a possible leave date as a reason to check the notes column, not as confirmation that leave applies to a particular person.

Keep the rear loading door in the review because it has a specific delivery purpose. Do not turn the quoted remark about that door into a new restriction.

## Discussion remarks and handoff note

If the proposal refers to the discussion, include these remarks exactly as quoted. They are practical comments and worries, not a formal vote or evidence of unanimous agreement:

- “The rear door is for carts, not a shortcut after midnight.”
- “I can cover the Tuesday close, but I can't own every badge question.”
- “Please don't delete a name just because the log is quiet.”

Retain this coordinator handoff note exactly and in full. It suggests a cross-check; it does not mean every paused person should be contacted:

“Nia: compare the Current and Paused tabs before sending review reminders; a leave date may be in the notes column.”

## Sample record and final section

Include a small sample review record using clearly fictional placeholder values only. Do not use any real person’s name, email, phone number, or badge ID, and do not create an entry for the visiting photographer or anyone else. Include fields corresponding to name, email, phone number, badge ID, door scope, sponsor, and review date. Show an unknown value as needing follow-up rather than guessing.

End with a substantive section of unresolved questions or information to confirm. Include who can make an access change, who can serve as backup maintainer, how blank sponsors should be resolved, and what to do when a badge record conflicts with the tabs. Leave these as open questions; do not supply answers. Do not claim that the process has been approved or decide who gets access. The result should be easy for Nia and the closing staff to understand and use."}]
